description: Four rules, and only four.
GROUP WHAT ONLY WORKS TOGETHER. A bot bumped the Compose compiler alone
and broke the build, because that version is only meaningful paired with
Kotlin:
e: This version (1.5.15) of the Compose Compiler requires Kotlin version
1.9.25 but you appear to be using Kotlin version 1.9.24
STAY ON LATEST OTHERWISE. This project has no installed base to keep
working and CI builds the APK, compiles the iOS app and bundles the Worker
on every PR — so a major that breaks something says so in minutes. Holding
majors back for review would be buying safety CI already provides, and
paying for it in a permanent backlog of deferred upgrades.
PIN EVERYTHING; NO RANGES. rangeStrategy: pin, so package.json names an
exact version and every change to what we run is a diff somebody can read.
A caret hides the update inside the lock file: `wrangler: ^4.0.0` had
quietly become 4.127.1, and the manifest still claimed 4.0.0 — a hundred
and twenty-seven minor versions that no PR title ever mentioned. It also
makes the two files say the same thing, so `npm ci` and `npm install` can
no longer disagree about what this project depends on.
LET A RELEASE SOAK. minimumReleaseAge holds an update back for three days
before it is proposed at all. Not for stability: this project pins every
version and CI builds the APK, the iOS app and the Worker on every pull
request, so a version that is merely broken says so in minutes.
It is for the supply chain. The npm and Actions attacks of the last few
years share one shape: a malicious version is published, and it is found
and pulled within hours to a couple of days. The repository that updates
within the hour is the one that catches it; three days is somebody else
finding it first.
It matters MOST where automerge is on. A grouped GitHub Actions patch
merges with nobody reading it, so the soak is the only thing standing
between this repository and a version that was compromised at breakfast
and yanked by lunch.
A SECURITY FIX STILL DOES NOT WAIT. vulnerabilityAlerts overrides it to
nothing, because the reasoning inverts: there the known-bad version is the
one already installed, and three days is three days of running it.

packageRules.description: Kotlin and the Compose compiler plugin are released together and only work together. Never separately, ever.
The AndroidX stack moves as a set. compose-bom exists precisely to keep these in step, so bumping one at a time defeats the point of it.
AGP and Gradle have a supported-version matrix. A new AGP frequently requires a newer Gradle, so they arrive together or the build fails on the first one.

compileSdk and minSdk are not dependencies. Raising them opts into platform behaviour and needs the matching SDK installed on every builder — including the one in android.yml. That is a coordinated change across three files, so it stays a person's job.
Actions are grouped and automerged on patch/minor: they are covered by every workflow run, so a break is visible immediately and revertible in one click.
package.json's engines floor is a compatibility claim about what the code needs, not a statement about what CI runs. Renovate moves the runner; a person moves the claim.
Dev-only type checking. Grouped because @types/node and typescript are only meaningful against each other.
wrangler is the deploy tool for the coordinator; a major version can change wrangler.toml's schema.
The guest agent's pull request needs its file pinned by hand (the custom manager above says why), so it says how.
prBodyNotes: **Before merging:** run `node scripts/pin-guest-agent.mjs` on this branch and commit what it writes. Renovate moved the version; that script pins the file (address, size, SHA-256) and refuses a build that will not run on the images here. CI stays red until it has.

description: OPNsense, read from its vendor's directory listing.

THE SOAK IS KEPT, ONE STEP LATER. The listing carries no release dates and its names carry none either (26.1.3 says nothing about when), and Renovate 42 and later hold an update with no date back for good under minimumReleaseAge, so these would never be proposed. They are proposed at once instead, and what the soak protects against is held at the pin: a release is pinned by a person, after three days (the note below). Nothing reaches a machine before CI is green, and CI is red until the pin is written.
The cloud images used to be here too, until somebody pointed out that 20261015-2632 is a date. Their datasources below read it, so they soak like everything else.

packageRules.description: Ubuntu's releases are release-<date>, with a .<n> when one was published twice in a day.
OPNsense's releases are named by its nano image, the one the edge is built from.
The cloud images' pull request needs the rest of the pin written, so it says how.
prBodyNotes: **Before merging:** run `node scripts/pin-images.mjs` on this branch and commit what it writes. Renovate moved the build; that script pins its address, digest and sizes from the vendor's own checksum file. It also refuses a build whose checksum file is younger than three days, saying when it can be pinned, which should not happen here (this pull request waited for that already) and is a thing to look into if it does. CI stays red until it has run.

packageRules.description: A new OPNsense release is a new file system under the edge router's configuration, so its pull request is a person's work, and it says what that is.
prBodyNotes: **A person pins this, after three days.** For the new release, in `src/fleet/host/edge-router.js` `OPNSENSE_IMAGE`: the nano image's `url`, its `sha256` from `OPNsense-<release>-checksums-amd64.sha256`, `compressedSize`, and `rawSize` (the unpacked size). Then unpack it (`bzip2 -dc … > nano.img`), find `/usr/local/etc/config.xml` and write its `config` offset, length and SHA-256, and run `node scripts/opnsense-room.mjs nano.img <inode>` for `grow`. Read `EDGE_FILTER`'s blocklist keys and rule file names again from the release's own models. Set `checked` to the release last. CI stays red until the address and `checked` both name it.

**What changed upstream:** [OPNsense {{{newMajor}}}.{{{newMinor}}} release notes](https://docs.opnsense.org/releases/CE_{{{newMajor}}}.{{{newMinor}}}.html), which also cover its point releases. The mirror the version is read from lists files and nothing else, so Renovate cannot find these by itself.

packageRules.description: The installer follows the fork's master by commit, and git-refs gives no dates, so it is proposed at once and its soak is kept by scripts/pin-xo-installer.mjs, which refuses a commit younger than three days. Its pull request needs that script run.
prBodyNotes: **Before merging:** run `node scripts/pin-xo-installer.mjs` on this branch and commit what it writes. Renovate moved the commit; that script pins `base` and the SHA-256 of every file the deploy reads at it, and refuses a commit younger than three days. CI stays red until it has. Read what changed upstream too: this script is run as root in a VM made with the pool's admin sign-in.

**What changed upstream:** [{{{currentDigestShort}}}…{{{newDigestShort}}}](https://github.com/00o-sh/XenOrchestraInstallerUpdater/compare/{{{currentDigest}}}...{{{newDigest}}}). The fork has no tags, releases or changelog, so these commits are the whole record.

packageRules.description: The sandbox's Node major: whole LTS lines only, the even majors, read from the node-version datasource as a major alone.

description: A security fix does not wait for anything, and that now includes the soak.
The reasoning inverts here. Everywhere else the risk is a NEW version
nobody has looked at yet; in an advisory the known-bad version is the one
already installed, and three days of soaking is three more days of
running it.
Debian's cloud images, one directory per build (20261001-2618/), as the listing at cloud.debian.org links them. depName is the release's codename.

THE DATE IS IN THE NAME. The listing itself carries none, and without one Renovate 42 and later hold an update back for good under minimumReleaseAge. So the transform keeps the links that are builds and reads each one's day out of its first eight digits, as the last second of that day in UTC: a build named for a day cannot have been published before it, so the soak that follows is never shorter than the three days everything else gets. scripts/pin-images.mjs still checks the checksum file's own date when it pins, as the second line.
Ubuntu's cloud images, one directory per release (release-20260926/), as cloud-images.ubuntu.com links them. depName is the release's codename.
The date is in the name here too, after release-, and is read the same way as Debian's above and for the same reason; a .1 after it is a second build of the same day and keeps that day.

opnsense.description: OPNsense's installer images on its own mirror, whose nano image the edge router is built from.

description: The nvm release install/prereq.sh fetches. It is a URL in a shell script,
which no manager knows how to read — so the version is annotated in place
and matched here.
It matters more than an ordinary pin: that script runs as root and pipes
nvm's installer into bash. An unpinned ref would be arbitrary code from a
moving target, and a pinned one nobody bumps is a known-old one. Renovate
is what makes 'pinned' and 'current' the same thing.
The Claude Code version the sandbox image bakes in and the fleet hosts
install. It was already annotated in the Containerfile, but nothing read
that comment: the only customManager here is scoped to install/prereq.sh,
and Renovate's Dockerfile manager reads FROM lines, not an arbitrary npm
version in an ARG. So the pin sat at 2.1.234 while npm reached 2.1.282 -
forty-eight releases that no PR ever mentioned.
The three host installs were worse: unpinned, so every runner build took
whatever was latest that morning and the fleet ran a different version
from the image it is supposed to mirror. Two of them now live in
TheTechNetwork/Fleetwright-Runners-Template, whose renovate.json pins them.
mac-host.yml carried the same comment and was not in this list, so it sat at 2.1.283 while the image moved on.
The Node the deb carries in /usr/lib/fleetwright/node. Shipping a runtime
is only better than nvm or NodeSource if it moves, and this is what moves
it: a Node security release arrives as a PR like any other dependency,
and vulnerabilityAlerts above means it does not wait out the soak.
versioning=node, so it follows LTS lines only. A Current release is not
stable by Renovate's definition until its line reaches LTS, which is the
right bar for a runtime shipped to machines nobody is watching.
The Renovate the config check runs, in .github/workflows/renovate-config.yml.
Pinned there because @latest stopped installing at 44.131.1; this keeps the
pin moving, one pull request at a time, each checked by the version it proposes.
The Xen guest agent every machine image carries, GUEST_AGENT in
src/fleet/host/vm-image.js, from upstream's GitLab releases.
Renovate moves the version and nothing else: the file's address is a CI
job number, not the version, and upstream publishes no digest, so no
datasource can say what the new file is. scripts/pin-guest-agent.mjs
writes that half (address, size, SHA-256) from the release's own asset
link, after checking the binary runs on every image here. Until it has
run, the version and the file disagree and the pull request is red,
which is the point: a bumped name with an old digest would build
without the agent and nobody would be told why.
The cloud images' builds, DEBIAN_IMAGE and UBUNTU_* in src/fleet/host/vm-image.js, and the OPNsense release in src/fleet/host/edge-router.js, each annotated in place.

Renovate moves the name and nothing else: the address, digest and sizes are the build's, and no datasource gives them. scripts/pin-images.mjs writes them for the cloud images; OPNsense's are a person's (the package rule above says what). Until then the name and the address disagree and test/pin-images.test.js is red, which is the point: a moved name with an old digest would download the old image, or refuse the new one, and nobody would be told why.

customManagers.description: The OPNsense release the edge router is built from, OPNSENSE_IMAGE.release in src/fleet/host/edge-router.js.

description: The Xen Orchestra installer an XO deploy runs, INSTALLER in src/fleet/host/xo-deploy.js: a commit of the fork that carries the disk.importContent fix, following its master.

Renovate moves the commit and nothing else. The deploy checks every file it reads against a SHA-256 pinned beside the commit, and those follow from the commit, so scripts/pin-xo-installer.mjs writes them, and `base`. Until it has run `base` names another commit and test/pin-xo-installer.test.js is red.
Named `xo-installer`, with the git URL as packageName, because Renovate puts the name in its commit subject and the URL made it 92 characters, which commitlint rejects at 80.

The Node every workflow sets up, `node-version:` under actions/setup-node. The github-actions manager reads `uses:` and not an action's inputs, so these sat where they were written while install/deb/node.env moved. Exact versions only: the CI matrix's bare majors are a person's choice of which lines to test.

customManagers.description: The JDK setup-java installs, in Adoptium's own version format, which is what the java-version datasource reads.
Images a workflow runs with `docker run`, which no manager reads: only `container:` and `services:` are. By number, never by codename, so a new release is a version Renovate can see.
The Swift packages the iOS app builds with, under `packages:` in apps/ios/project.yml. XcodeGen writes the project from it, and no manager reads XcodeGen's spec.
The Node line the sandbox image takes from nodesource, a major alone, because nodesource's setup script is named by one.
